title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The 'dualité de Killing' step g/Ω ≅ ℒ^∨ fails as stated in characteristic 2: the Killing form of sl2 is 4·tr(xy), so it vanishes there. The isomorphism itself survives in all characteristics, either through the trace form on M or directly from the filtration, but not through the Killing form. Grothendieck flags char 2 himself on the previous page.
Identifying g with g' (and ℒ with ℒ') requires 2 invertible. The note says so, but the list a)–e') is presented as equivalent without that caveat attached to d/d'.
The note asserts ℒ = f_*L ≅ f_*(L/J^2L) without justification. It is correct: degree 1 on the fibres plus restriction to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of σ.
Minor: Fil_2 is first written ≅ Ω⊗ℒ, then ≅ ℒ. The intermediate should read Ω^{-1}⊗(Ω·ℒ) ≅ ℒ. This is a notational slip, not a mathematical error.

missed.claim: Around 1972, Grothendieck set up a scheme-theoretic, characteristic-sensitive theory of P^1-bundles with section and connection: the oper/indigenous-bundle formalism. He did this explicitly to study Picard–Fuchs equations and the Cartier operation. That is the same circle of ideas later developed by Mochizuki (dormant indigenous bundles, char-p uniformisation) and in the oper literature. The page itself only sets up the dictionary, but the intended link between opers, Gauss–Manin connections and the Cartier operator is not credited to Grothendieck anywhere I know of.
missed.quote: Supposons X/S, et considérons des connexions rel. S sur les objets des types envisagés dans 1.1 ... (P, σ, ∇) ... Il nous sera particulièrement commode d'expliciter en termes de (ℒ, Ω)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the oper/indigenous-bundle viewpoint on Picard–Fuchs equations in positive characteristic. The following pages of cote 93 should be checked for whether he reached dormancy (p-curvature zero) or Frobenius-related statements.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra on this page is standard: Borel reductions of PGL2-bundles and the root filtration of the adjoint bundle. The interest is historical. It shows Grothendieck building the indigenous-bundle/oper formalism over general bases, with characteristic-2 care, in a Picard–Fuchs plus Cartier-operation context years before Drinfeld–Sokolov, Beilinson–Drinfeld and Mochizuki. This page only prepares that and contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: '𝔤 = [-...-] Lie de σ(X) dans P' should most likely read 'Ω = conormal de σ(X) dans P' (Ω ≅ J/J^2). This fits ℒ ≅ σ*P^1(L).
'torseurs sous H^1(ℒ) défini par l'extension' should likely read 'torseurs sous W(Ω) (or V(Ω)) défini par l'extension': the class lies in H^1(X, Ω).
In 1.7 a), 'section transversale σ' should probably just read 'avec section σ'. The struck word near e') appears to be 'transversal(e)'.

c) likely reads 'Algèbre d'Azumaya de rang 4 M, avec idéal [à gauche] spécial'. This matches 1.1 c) on the previous page and 'M = End ℒ avec idéal annulateur de Ω' further down, rather than 'algèbre d'opérateurs d'ordre ≤ 2 ... Ω^2'.
f) appears to read 'Une O_X-Algèbre augmentée P_2, de rang 2(?), d'idéal I, à I^2 = 0 (or I^3?)'. This is the sheaf of principal parts along σ, consistent with f_*(L/J^2L).
'G' = SL(ℒ)' seems right. The centre divided out to get (G, B) is μ_2.
